game.intro: The first sliver of moon is back. Ease in gently, get close, and do not go over. Saturn is watching the line.
game.question: How many letters are in the Greek alphabet, alpha through omega?
game.source: Standard modern Greek alphabet: 24 letters, alpha to omega.

game.intro: Moon in Pisces, brain in a puddle. Three quick picks before the daydream floats away.
DES alert: the clocks have been gossiping behind your backs. Saturn wants to know which one squealed.
game.question: Which clock in your home is most likely to spill your secrets?

game.intro: Deep breath before the cannonball. Saturn has his towel ready. Get dangerously close to something round.
game.prompt: Something in your house that is round, a bit heavy, and would make an excellent splash.

game.intro: The moon is in Aries and the Tiger has the house keys. Saturn has hidden the spares. Be wrong with confidence.
game.question: What do you call a baby kangaroo?

game.intro: Mid-month clipboard check. Saturn would like you to know he can hear you not filing things.
game.prompt: Saturn flipping through his clipboard, clicking his pen and sighing at your paperwork.

game.intro: The Great Slow Saturday. Nobody is rushing. Saturn is still in his robe. Spell us something delicious.
game.prompt: Your perfect slow Saturday breakfast, course by course.

game.intro: A jar lid has won again. Patience is the theme, revenge is the subtext. Two truths and one tall tale, please.
game.prompt: Three household objects that have personally defeated you. One of them is made up.

game.intro: Moon in Gemini means two conversations at once. Saturn will be listening to both. Quick picks!
Today is the day of the second question. Saturn has many. He'll start with this one.
game.question: If the universe let you ask it one follow-up question, which would you pick?

game.intro: Don't even scream: two puzzle pieces, two houses, one perfect fit. Show us the half and make them guess.
game.prompt: One of two things in your home that fit together perfectly. Shoot it so close it's a mystery.

game.intro: The porch light moon is on, full and bright in Cancer. Saturn left it on for you. Now be beautifully wrong.
game.question: What is the main job of a lighthouse?

game.intro: Full moon in Leo! Ruby and onyx are recharging on the sill and the studio lion wants a turn at the mic.
game.prompt: A lion trying to roar politely so it doesn't wake the neighbours.

game.intro: The moon is still full and still bowing. Nobody asked for an encore. It's doing one anyway.
game.headline: FULL MOON REFUSES TO LEAVE THE STAGE, DEMANDS ___ FOR ITS ENCORE

game.intro: Sock drawer reckoning day. Focus up: the closest guess without going over takes the trophy and the spare socks.
game.question: How many cards are in a full standard tarot deck, Major and Minor Arcana together?
game.source: Standard tarot deck: 22 Major Arcana + 56 Minor Arcana = 78 (the style guide's own card list).

game.intro: A button is hanging by one thread and so is Saturn's patience. Rest day rules: answer fast, then nap.
Moon in Libra, scales perfectly even. Saturn is making a crossing and needs to know what you're weighing.
game.question: The universe hands you a perfectly balanced scale. What goes on it first?

game.intro: Half moon, half price, half everything. Saturn signs the peace treaty and wants to see your better half.
game.prompt: Something in your kitchen that comes in halves.

game.intro: Don't even scream: three hearts and an octopus. Saturn is counting arms and would like your wildest count.
game.question: How many arms does an octopus have?

game.intro: There's a sealed envelope on the judges' desk. Saturn won't open it until he hears your most dramatic version.
game.prompt: An envelope being opened very, very slowly, like the results of a contest of utmost importance.

game.intro: Nor'easter incoming! The crew has taped the windows and Saturn is wearing two toques. Spell us your plan.
game.prompt: Your full nor'easter survival plan, from first flake to final shovel.

game.intro: Last page of January. Saturn is closing the book but first he wants one good fib for the margins.
game.prompt: Three things that happened to you this January. One of them is pure fiction.

game.intro: Twenty Twenty-Seven is open for business and the crew already blew a noisemaker in Saturn's ear. Warm up those pipes.
game.prompt: A party popper that misfired at 12:01 and is now quietly embarrassed about it.

game.intro: Confetti in the couch, confetti in the boots. Saturn has declared a rest day and is lying face down on the judges' desk.
game.prompt: Something you found under the couch cushions after the holidays.

game.intro: A mitten came home today after weeks at sea. In honour of its return, Saturn wants your finest lost-and-found lies.
game.prompt: Three things you lost and later found again. One of them never happened.

game.intro: The compass is spinning, the moon is in Sagittarius, and you have ten seconds per choice. No dithering, Tiger.
Don't even scream: a narwhal, in this economy? Saturn has spilled his coffee. Pick yours, then guess theirs.
game.question: A narwhal surfaces in the harbour and offers you exactly one favour. What do you ask for?
options: A tusk-guided tour of the bay
A ride back to the shore

game.intro: New moon in Capricorn: the Mountain gets the dark sky all to herself. Bring us something that fights the dark.
game.prompt: Something in your home that glows in the dark, or at least tries really hard.

game.intro: Zero percent moon tonight. Saturn says that's suspicious and wants your most confident nonsense on the record.
game.question: How many moons does Earth have?

game.intro: The moon packs its bags and leaves Capricorn. Somewhere a plow driver hums. Give us the full opera.
game.prompt: A snowplow passing your window at 5 am, performed as a dramatic opera solo.

game.intro: Welcome to the Snow Day Inventors' Fair! Saturn judged the potato cannon and is still picking spuds out of his rings.
game.headline: SNOW DAY INVENTOR UNVEILS ___, SHOVELS EVERYWHERE FILE FORMAL COMPLAINT
